drafts.title: Voice control reliably executes common driving commands while driving
drafts.description: When driving, the driver can speak common in-car commands (navigation destination, call contact, play music, climate basics) and the car reliably understands and executes them without repeated attempts.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a vehicle cabin noise profile up to 70 dB(A), the system recognizes and correctly executes at least 95% of a standardized set of 40 common driving-related commands across 50 test drivers in 100 test runs.
assumptions: Standardized command set and test protocol agreed with UX and QA teams.
Speech tests cover major US English accents; cloud assistance may be available in tests where connectivity is present.
uncertainties: Performance variation for heavy accents or non-English languages.
Behavior when the vehicle is offline vs. online (may lower accuracy).

drafts.title: Wireless charging pad consistently keeps phones charging while driving
drafts.description: When a phone is placed on the vehicle's wireless charging pad in normal use (including short phone movements and incoming calls/notifications), it remains charging without intermittent disconnects through typical drives.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: For 95% of the top 30 phone models by US market share (with cases ≤4 mm), a phone placed on the pad maintains a positive charging state (battery level does not drop due to charger disconnect) continuously for a 90-minute continuous driving test and during simulated incoming calls/notifications.
assumptions: Phones tested follow Qi charging standard and are placed by users within a normal placement tolerance defined by UX team.
Test set of phone models is representative of the US market at vehicle launch.
uncertainties: Extreme cases (thick metal cases, large magnetic mounts) may still cause failures.
Behavior for future phone models after launch.

drafts.title: Physical temperature and fan controls operable eyes‑free
drafts.description: Drivers can change temperature and fan speed using tactile physical controls without looking at the control cluster.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In usability testing, users can (1) change cabin temperature by at least ±1.0°C and (2) increase or decrease fan speed by one step within 2 seconds while keeping eyes on the road in at least 90% of attempts.
assumptions: Controls are placed within ergonomic reach and have distinct tactile differences (knobs/buttons) to support eyes-free operation.
uncertainties: Exact placement and shape that maximise blind discoverability will require iterative ergonomic testing.

drafts.title: Head‑up display and center screen remain legible in bright sunlight
drafts.description: Drivers can read essential information on both the head‑up display and the center screen in bright sunlight without repositioning or shading the windshield.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Critical driving or navigation information on the HUD and the center screen is legible to 90% of test participants at an ambient illumination of 80,000 lux (direct sunlight scenario) while seated in typical driver positions and wearing common sunglasses.
assumptions: Ambient illumination target of 80,000 lux represents strong direct sunlight conditions for the test protocol.
Legibility is measured using a standard legibility chart of typical HUD and center-screen content (speed, navigation turn, caller ID).
uncertainties: Extreme sun angles or aftermarket windshield tints may still impair legibility.
Trade-offs between display luminance and night-time comfort need validation.

drafts.title: Customers can view, export and permanently delete their saved driver profile data from the vehicle
drafts.description: Owners can inspect what personal data the vehicle holds in their driver profile, obtain a downloadable copy, and permanently remove that personal data from the vehicle and linked local sessions.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: A driver can (1) generate and download a complete export of their local driver profile data within 2 minutes in 95% of attempts, and (2) permanently delete the driver profile locally such that auto-login and local personalization do not restore the profile in subsequent sessions in 95% of verification attempts.
assumptions: Export may use temporary connectivity to a user-controlled device or cloud; local deletion removes local profile artifacts and prevents immediate re-provisioning from local caches.
Backend and dealer workflows will support requests that require server-side deletion where applicable.
uncertainties: Exact deletion and export semantics when profiles are synchronized to cloud accounts depend on third-party service agreements.
Timing for complete deletion if server-side actions are required.

drafts.title: Heated steering wheel is included as content of the Cold Weather package
drafts.description: The heated steering wheel is offered as part of the Cold Weather package so customers who buy that package receive the heated wheel without adding it separately.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: For the US-market configurator and build cards at launch, the Cold Weather package includes the heated steering wheel as standard content for at least 90% of available trims/options where Cold Weather package is offered.
assumptions: This requirement targets the US market where customers most frequently request this package composition.
Product and options documentation will reflect the package composition at homologation.
uncertainties: Some specialized trims or performance variants may have packaging constraints that prevent inclusion.

drafts.title: Request that the vehicle infotainment passes CCC (China Compulsory Certification)
drafts.description: Customers asked that the infotainment system passes CCC certification for the Chinese market.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This is a regulatory/certification request and therefore tracked as out of scope for product feature requirements.
assumptions: CCC is a homologation requirement handled by certification and engineering compliance teams.
drafts.scope_reason: Certification and homologation requests (CCC) are regulatory activities and out of scope for product feature requirements.

drafts.title: Request that the driver profile satisfies every GDPR requirement (regulatory request)
drafts.description: Customers asked that the driver profile implementation satisfies GDPR requirements for data storage — this is a compliance/regulatory demand.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This is a regulatory/compliance request and therefore tracked as out of scope for product feature requirements.
assumptions: GDPR compliance is a legal/regulatory responsibility requiring legal and compliance verification beyond product UX requirements.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory and legal compliance requests (GDPR) are out of scope for product feature drafts; feature-level data controls were created separately to address customer data-control needs.

drafts.title: Request that the cockpit computer use the Snapdragon 8295 chip (engineering specification)
drafts.description: Customers requested a specific SoC (Snapdragon 8295) for the cockpit computer.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This is an engineering-level component request and therefore out of scope for customer-facing product requirements.
assumptions: Component selection is an engineering implementation detail handled by hardware and platform teams.
drafts.scope_reason: Requests for specific chips or parts are engineering specifications and out of scope for customer-facing requirements.

drafts.title: Requests about base price, lease rates and other financing terms (out of scope)
drafts.description: Customers requested a lower base price, cheaper lease rates, 0% financing and other price/finance changes.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Pricing, monthly lease rates, and financing terms are commercial decisions and therefore out of scope for product feature requirements.
assumptions: Pricing and finance offerings are decided by commercial and finance organizations.
drafts.scope_reason: Requests that concern vehicle price, lease rates or financing terms are commercial/financial and out of scope for product feature requirements.

drafts.title: Requests for package pricing adjustments, free packages or dealer margin changes (out of scope)
drafts.description: Customers asked that packages be free, that particular packages be discounted (e.g., Comfort package -30%), and that dealers earn lower margins on optional extras.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Package pricing and dealer margins are commercial decisions and therefore out of scope for product feature requirements.
assumptions: Package price decisions and dealer compensation are commercial/policy matters handled outside product requirement specifications.
drafts.scope_reason: Requests about package prices, discounts or dealer margins are commercial decisions and out of scope for product feature requirements.

drafts.title: Request to offer heated seats as a subscription at $15/month (pricing/subscription request)
drafts.description: Customers asked that heated seats be offered as a subscription at a specified monthly price.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Subscription pricing requests are commercial decisions and therefore out of scope for product feature requirements.
assumptions: Subscription pricing and billing models require commercial, legal and backend billing decisions beyond product feature definition.
drafts.scope_reason: Requests for specific subscription prices are commercial decisions and out of scope for product feature requirements.
